# Independent Set47 retained-bout reference (audit candidate; not frozen)

This tree derives expected bytes from the frozen Set47 contract and unchanged pre47 independent Python sources. It never imports the project, reads new Set47 Go, or uses Set47 Go output as an expected value. Root must review and freeze the finished tree before runtime comparisons. The original runtime basis and v1 freeze remain preserved. The additive dependency freeze pins the prepared-view/raw-byte-index change at `e7d15b4e6be72a5f49b7cc38fe0bff8402cc09b3`; the later immutable binding records final Set46 implementation `5e6b36d37e30d573a3817e32315bb96f12e0968c` and release `5c11cbaf5f1e236ffb3e46504e551be6dc5c2d69`, with the same six Card/seed dependency hashes. These provenance updates change no arithmetic, DTO, seed or digest recipe. Card metadata500ms does not prove or widen the separately frozen and still unproven Bout250ms gate.

The planned finite cases are in the pinned `inputs/contracts/set47-reference-plan.md`. During authoring, a separately requested narrow security review of the Set46 prepared-view implementation occurred. That review supplied no expected arithmetic or new Set47 runtime input. Set47 transcript generation was paused during the helper's real-clock latency measurements.

## Independent inputs

`extract_inputs.py` preserves exact inherited source bytes and extracts only named JSON pointers from prior corpora/public artifacts. `input_index.json` records complete original SHA256, exact pointer, extraction encoding, subset SHA and size. The baseline extraction refuses changing existing inputs; `extract_dependency_inputs.py` records the separately authorized dependency snapshot. They are historical extraction scripts, not runtime or fixture import APIs. After later additive inputs, verify the retained inventory rather than rerunning an earlier stage over a newer inventory. Original46-input and subsequent60-input inventories remain exact in `inputs/provenance/`. The final65-input inventory includes the final dependency binding and frozen42 engine contract for its scalar-bound proof, plus the frozen40 per-field public manifest limits. Some external report basenames were later superseded by root; their exact originally copied bytes and origin hashes remain pinned by the corresponding freeze. No claim is made that every mutable external report basename still contains its prior version. No recursive earlier corpus tree is copied.

`common.py` hash-checks every input before imports. The manifest/DNA generator is the exact old independent module and its small frozen tables. Condition and calendar functions are selected by explicit AST function-name allowlists from exact old source bytes; no old generator entry point runs. The engine executes exactly the named pure functions/classes and literal constant nodes of frozen `reference_bout.py` c3247a0d856270cc5043b5767ace9f628b2efb9cd120d786773f9221d928bd7f. Exact selected-source extraction hashes and AST-allowlisted names are retained in the corpus. Seven selected inherited engine cases cover available full-fight methods, tied/adjacent decision scoring, and retain the old primitive control source/data. They remain inherited controls, not evidence that the new booked cases realize every rare method.

Canonical new JSON uses fixed typed field order, no whitespace/LF, escaped ASCII controls and HTML `<`, `>` and `&`, literal DEL, and exact signed-field exceptions. Existing engine commitments retain their old canonical encoder and unframed domains; all valid engine strings use the frozen safe table/identifier alphabet, so the canonical bytes coincide. New store/source/record domains retain the contract's LE32 length framing.

## Source provenance and limits

`genuine_set46_middle` is an independent hypothetical composition from one actual retained Set46 booking. Its card and chain arithmetic were previously verified independently; a separate retained proof addendum verifies all three actual cutoff admissions with normal Argon. Exact report/public-source hashes and public admission wrappers are pinned here. This reference does not rerun PoW. The current source has a retained conflict: its immutable original booking can supply deterministic arithmetic, but it cannot authorize a new successful Run. A modeled original-finality overlay and a current historical-conflict overlay are explicitly separate. No Set47 Run, store insertion, result authority or current chain state is inferred.

Ten additional cases are **structural model-only compact projections**: five classes, each with both attribution orders under sorted full ProspectIDs. Original independent WorkHash-derived manifest/DNA values are reused. Prospect/source-record/omitted-card evidence commitments are openly synthetic fixture labels; there is no invented admission proof or real card journal. Prime and late-decline cutoff inputs are covered; later run clocks can be after retirement while the Input remains at the original eligible cutoff. These cases exercise pure compact-source validation/composition, not the provenance of a complete authenticated CardRecord.

The compact source deliberately omits complete snapshot/signature/chain/card evidence. Its CardRecordDigest commits omitted bytes but does not prove them. The new pure validator checks only available fields/identities/manifest/condition facts. Native cheap transport cannot authenticate regenerated manifest/name/condition/engine facts; core full validation can. The corpus records this distinction as `context: core|transport`.

## Consumer schema

`bout_v1.json` contains:

- `compositions`: eleven named cases, each carrying provenance, card/bout Pins, original compact Source, complete Input/InputID, complete Result/ResultDigest, immutable Record/RecordDigest, canonical strings, original store times and current fixture Views.
- `dtos`: `{kind,name,fixture_index,context,value,canonical,sha256}`. `fixture_index` selects the expected Pin from `compositions`. Canonical strings are exact UTF-8/ASCII bytes without LF.
- `codec_cases`: `{name,kind,fixture_index,context,base,recipe,input_sha256,input_bytes,accept,canonical_ref}`. `base` indexes `dtos`. `canonical_ref` is a DTO index only when acceptance canonicalizes to those exact bytes; accepted distinct mutations carry their exact `canonical` string. Rehashed draw-count mutation has explicit core-refused versus transport-accepted controls: bounded transport cannot authenticate a random stream it does not execute. A case's accept bit is checked by the independent parser, not copied from Go.
- `protocol_cases`: full request/response plus the current View, Pin, original store times, expected prior Job and optional terminal canonical SHA. This tests command/captured-tuple correlation separately from standalone structural acceptance.
- `portrait_cases`: closed PortraitResponse plus selected Record reference, current View, known creation times and fresh Status. The SVG is an explicitly labeled placeholder; these cases test only structural envelope, immutable tuple, current-view/fresh-status and cache-hit refusal. They do not validate SVG renderer output or its content digest, and are not end-to-end successful portrait evidence.
- `identity_cases`, `state_cases`, `initialization_cases`, `calendar_cases`, and `calendar_refusals`. The original fixed formula-bound report is retained as an input; observed corpus sizes are reported separately and do not replace that maximum-shape proof. State/initialization cases are abstract models, not executed disk crashes or account/chain tests.

The finite mutation recipe grammar is closed: `identity`; `set(path,value)`; `set_many(edits)`; `remove(path)`; `reverse(path)`; `whitespace_reversed`; `duplicate_top(key)`; `escaped_key_duplicate`; `replace_once(old,new)`; `pad(bytes)`. Paths are JSON pointers with decimal array indexes and exact decoded object keys. `set` permits an explicit new last key for unknown-field controls; other intermediate paths must exist. Reversal changes only the selected existing array, never sorts malformed input into validity. `replace_once` operates on canonical bytes and must find its exact old substring. Padding is ASCII spaces after the complete canonical value. Helper request/response limits include one LF; standalone core caps do not. Every materialized control retains its exact byte hash/length; representative canonical DTO bytes are stored once rather than copying full transcripts into every mutation.

## Verification and honest evidence

The verifier regenerates canonical output in two Python versions with distinct hash seeds/timezones, checks every case and all input hashes before/after, and retains commands/timings/source hashes. It checks seven selected old engine cases exactly. No engine or source generator runs on transport-only validation: private traps enforce this separation. All3,861 Saturday cutoffs/deadlines are cross-checked using a separate Python standard-library calendar/timezone implementation reading only the exact pinned TZif, including its future POSIX rules; host timezone data is never substituted.

The small state model records only the specified local insert/replay/clock/capacity and uncertainty relations. It is not an exhaustive account/event/seed observation journal and does not claim an exact count of underlying synchronous writes. Metadata-only actions never simulate; one new successful or interrupted run can call the engine once; saved replay never rerolls. Synthetic capacity counts are not 256 proof-verified transcripts or measured startup performance.

No professional or exhibition W/L/D, XP, training, title, sale, result signing/publication, proof of unbiased seed selection, production activation, GUI rendering, native chooser, screen-reader or D74 acceptance is established. Actual Set47 closed-event execution and real-clock packaged behavior are separate later gates. Frozen predecessor references and genuine source artifacts remain unchanged.

The first self-check found a model-only chronology error: prime admission had been placed at cutoff, after its cutoff-minus-one roster assignment. Only synthetic birth/admission timestamps moved one millisecond earlier. The genuine source never changed. A second self-check found that accepted reversed-key Info retained the incoming nested Pin order; normalization now rebuilds Pin/BoutView and outer Snapshot response View in declared field order. These corrections came from frozen rules and Python self-checks, never Go outputs. Full earlier draft/source captures are retained outside this input tree at `set47-reference-draft-attempt1/` and `set47-reference-draft-attempt2/`. A third initially passing corpus is retained at `set47-reference-draft-attempt3/` before final provenance, scalar and correlation coverage additions.

The modeled state clock covers only the named local transition, not every source/account observation write or exact runtime refusal ordering. Modeled initialization recognizes absent/real-empty ResumePrepared, but does not execute crashes. No native SVG renderer or portrait content conformance is claimed by this corpus. Rare engine methods are inherited controls only; the new11 booked compositions need not realize them all.

The first dual-version check produced identical semantic arrays/transcripts but different Python AST dump metadata (3.9 versus3.14). That failed capture is retained at `set47-reference-repro-attempt1/`. Selection metadata now hashes the exact pinned source segments in source order, framed by LE32 lengths and names, while execution still uses the explicit AST allowlist. No expected fight, identity, codec acceptance or protocol value was changed by this portability correction.
